# Patient cohort

We use the internal neuroblastoma cohort `reanalysis.NB.bulkRNA`, processed by
Celine Prakash
(`/mnt/bioinformatics/Research/TASCHNERMANDL/Internal/data/reanalysis.NB.bulkRNA/celine_reanalysis_2023/analysis/nb-full_omics/`,
2023-11-17; details in `full_omics_analysis.html` there). Reads were trimmed
with fastp, quantified with salmon and summarised to genes with tximeta.
edgeR's `filterByExpr` kept 14,604 of 38,269 genes. Two matrices of these
normalised counts are used:

- `full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts_liblayout_corrected.csv`:
  limma's `removeBatchEffect` removed the library-layout effect (single-end
  unstranded, single-end stranded, paired-end), with the material kept in the
  design. Used for display only: the [ATRX-interactor](#atrx-interactors)
  boxplots and the PCAs.
- `full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts.csv`: the same values without
  the correction. Tested in the
  [differential expression](#differential-expression-atrxdel-mycnamp-and-atrxwtmycnwt),
  with the library layout in the model instead.

Nomenclature:

- **ATRXdel**: ATRX deletion. **MYCNamp**: MYCN amplification, ATRX wild type.
  **ATRXwtMYCNwt**: ATRX and MYCN wild type. **control**: bone marrow negative
  for tumour cells.
- **Tum**: primary tumour. **DTC**: disseminated tumour cells (bone marrow).
  **dx**: diagnosis. **TRE**: treatment. **rel**: relapse.

```{r cohort-data, results = "asis"}
# ── Inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# All three are patient data that stay on the cluster (params). Without the
# metadata every patient panel is skipped; without one matrix, only the part
# that needs it.
read_param <- function(f, ...)
  if (nzchar(f) && file.exists(f)) read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE, ...) else NULL
# The sample sheet, every column as text; NULL (with a note) if the file or
# one of the columns used is missing.
read_nb_meta <- function() {
  f <- params$nb_metadata
  if (!nzchar(f) || !file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  m <- as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(f, sheet = params$nb_metadata_sheet,
                                        col_types = "text"))
  need <- c("omics_id", "classification", "library_layout")
  if (!all(need %in% names(m))) {
    cat("\n> **Not available.** `", basename(f), "` lacks column(s) ",
        paste(setdiff(need, names(m)), collapse = ", "), ".\n\n", sep = "")
    return(NULL)
  }
  m <- m[!is.na(m$omics_id) & nzchar(trimws(m$omics_id)), , drop = FALSE]
  # Rename sheet IDs to the matrices' names (params$nb_id_prefix_alias).
  m$omics_id <- trimws(m$omics_id)
  for (from in names(params$nb_id_prefix_alias)) {
    hit <- startsWith(tolower(m$omics_id), paste0(tolower(from), "_"))
    if (any(hit)) {
      m$omics_id[hit] <- paste0(params$nb_id_prefix_alias[[from]],
                                substring(m$omics_id[hit], nchar(from) + 1))
      cat(sprintf("\n%d sample IDs in `%s` renamed from `%s_…` to `%s_…` to match the expression matrices.\n\n",
                  sum(hit), basename(f), from, params$nb_id_prefix_alias[[from]]))
    }
  }
  m
}
nb_meta   <- read_nb_meta()
nb_expr   <- read_param(params$nb_expression, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)  # layout-corrected
nb_counts <- read_param(params$nb_counts, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)      # as tested
if (is.null(nb_meta)) {
  cat("\n> **Not available.** `params$nb_metadata` was not found; every patient",
      "panel is skipped.\n\n")
  nb_expr <- nb_counts <- NULL
} else {
  if (is.null(nb_expr))
    cat("\n> **Not available.** `params$nb_expression` (layout-corrected matrix) was",
        "not found: no patient boxplots, and no layout-corrected PCA.\n\n")
  if (is.null(nb_counts))
    cat("\n> **Not available.** `params$nb_counts` (uncorrected matrix) was not",
        "found: no differential expression.\n\n")
}

# ── Groups, categories and the differential-expression analyses ──────────────
NB_STATUS    <- c("ATRXdel", "MYCNamp", "ATRXwtMYCNwt", "control")
NB_CATEGORY  <- c("Tum dx", "Tum TRE", "Tum rel", "DTC dx", "DTC TRE", "DTC rel", "control")
NB_TIMEPOINT <- c(DX = "dx", TRE = "TRE", REL = "rel")  # third field of omics_id
# The control bone marrow is not the same cells: shown in the boxplots, never tested.
NB_TUMOUR <- c("ATRXdel", "MYCNamp", "ATRXwtMYCNwt")
NB_GROUPS <- NB_TUMOUR
# EDIT: the five sample sets, each one differential-expression analysis and
# one box per group in the ATRX-interactor plots (label = the box's name).
# categories = NULL takes every tumour category.
NB_SETS <- list(
  all_combined = list(title = "All tumour samples",           label = "All tumour",
                      categories = NULL),
  tumour_dx    = list(title = "Primary tumour, diagnosis",    label = "Tum dx",
                      categories = "Tum dx"),
  BM_pooled    = list(title = "Bone marrow (DTC), all timepoints", label = "DTC all",
                      categories = c("DTC dx", "DTC TRE", "DTC rel")),
  BM_dx        = list(title = "Bone marrow (DTC), diagnosis", label = "DTC dx",
                      categories = "DTC dx"),
  BM_relapse   = list(title = "Bone marrow (DTC), relapse",   label = "DTC rel",
                      categories = "DTC rel"))
# A set's samples (NULL categories = every tumour category).
nb_set_samples <- function(d, set)
  if (is.null(set$categories)) d else d[d$category %in% set$categories, , drop = FALSE]
NB_EXPR_MIN <- 1  # log2 scale: a gene is tested where above this in enough samples
# Okabe-Ito colours: distinct from the cell-line condition palette.
NB_GROUP_COL  <- c(ATRXdel = "#D55E00", MYCNamp = "#0072B2", ATRXwtMYCNwt = "#009E73")
NB_LAYOUT_COL <- c("#CC79A7", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#999999")

# ── One sample selection for the whole report ────────────────────────────────
# Sample columns of each matrix. The uncorrected matrix may carry its gene IDs
# in a named, blank or missing column; its samples are its numeric columns.
nb_matrices <- list()
if (!is.null(nb_expr))
  nb_matrices[[basename(params$nb_expression)]] <-
    setdiff(colnames(nb_expr), c("GeneID", "gene_name"))
if (!is.null(nb_counts))
  nb_matrices[[basename(params$nb_counts)]] <-
    names(nb_counts)[vapply(nb_counts, is.numeric, logical(1))]

# A sample whose classification is blank or not one of NB_STATUS is left out
# with that value as its reason; the rules below catch the rest.
NB_REASONS <- c(
  tissue    = "tumour classification, but tissue not TUM or DTC",
  timepoint = "no timepoint (not DX, TRE or REL)",
  layout    = "no library_layout (a covariate of the differential expression)")

nb_select <- function(meta, matrices) {
  clean <- function(x) trimws(ifelse(is.na(x), "", x))
  m <- data.frame(omics_id = clean(meta$omics_id),
                  classification = clean(meta$classification),
                  layout = clean(meta$library_layout), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  # omics_id is TISSUE_PATIENT_TIMEPOINT_N, e.g. DTC_021_REL_2.
  parts <- strsplit(m$omics_id, "_", fixed = TRUE)
  piece <- function(i) toupper(vapply(parts, function(x) if (length(x) >= i) x[i] else "", ""))
  m$tissue  <- piece(1)
  m$patient <- piece(2)
  m$tp      <- piece(3)
  # Classification matched ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, so
  # "Control" or "ATRXwt MYCNwt" still count; anything else is left out with
  # its value as the reason.
  norm <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", x))
  m$status <- NB_STATUS[match(norm(m$classification), norm(NB_STATUS))]
  # MNCs and cell lines without one of these classifications are not part of
  # the cohort: left out silently. Classified ones stay (a control may well be
  # an MNC sample).
  m <- m[!(m$tissue %in% c("MNC", "CL") & is.na(m$status)), ]
  type <- c(TUM = "Tum", DTC = "DTC")[m$tissue]
  m$category <- ifelse(
    m$status %in% "control", "control",
    ifelse(!is.na(type) & m$tp %in% names(NB_TIMEPOINT),
           paste(type, NB_TIMEPOINT[m$tp]), NA_character_))
  # Missing from a matrix, named after the file(s): every sample used must be
  # in both, so the boxplots and the tests see the same samples.
  miss <- character(nrow(m))
  for (f in names(matrices)) {
    a <- !m$omics_id %in% matrices[[f]]
    miss[a] <- ifelse(nzchar(miss[a]), paste(miss[a], "and", f), f)
  }
  m$reason <- case_when(
    nzchar(miss)                        ~ paste0("not in ", miss, " (e.g. dropped for low depth)"),
    !nzchar(m$classification)           ~ "no classification",
    is.na(m$status)                     ~ paste("classification:", m$classification),
    m$status != "control" & is.na(type) ~ NB_REASONS[["tissue"]],
    is.na(m$category)                   ~ NB_REASONS[["timepoint"]],
    m$status != "control" & !nzchar(m$layout) ~ NB_REASONS[["layout"]],
    TRUE                                ~ NA_character_)
  m
}

# cohort: every classified sample, with its reason if left out.
# box_samples: the ATRX-interactor boxplots (the tumour samples and the control).
# nb_de_samples: the differential expression (the same tumour samples).
cohort <- box_samples <- nb_de_samples <- NULL
if (!is.null(nb_meta) && length(nb_matrices)) {
  cohort <- nb_select(nb_meta, nb_matrices)
  box_samples   <- cohort[is.na(cohort$reason), ]
  nb_de_samples <- cohort[is.na(cohort$reason) & cohort$status %in% NB_TUMOUR, ]
}
```

## Groups and categories

Every sample is placed by three fields:

- **Group**: the `classification` column of `metadata_table_wStage.xlsx`
  (ATRXdel, MYCNamp, ATRXwtMYCNwt or control, matched ignoring case, spaces and
  punctuation). Any other value, or none, leaves the sample out. MNC and
  cell-line (`CL_`) samples without one of these groups are not part of the
  cohort and are not listed.
- **Category**: tissue and timepoint, the first and third fields of the sample
  ID (`TISSUE_PATIENT_TIMEPOINT_N`, e.g. `DTC_021_REL_2`): primary tumour (Tum)
  or bone marrow (DTC), at diagnosis, treatment or relapse. Control samples
  form a single category. A tumour sample of another tissue, or without a
  timepoint, is left out.
- **Patient**: the second field of the sample ID.

The same samples are used throughout the report. A sample must be in both
expression matrices, and a tumour sample needs a `library_layout`, the
covariate of the differential expression. The boxplots and the differential
expression use the same tumour samples, grouped into the same five sample sets
(next section); the control bone marrow is shown in the boxplots but never
tested.

```{r cohort-groups, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(cohort)) {
  used <- cohort[is.na(cohort$reason), ]
  by_cell <- list(factor(used$status, NB_STATUS), factor(used$category, NB_CATEGORY))

  # Patients per group and category.
  n_tab <- tapply(used$patient, by_cell, function(p) length(unique(p)))
  n_tab[is.na(n_tab)] <- 0L
  n_tab <- n_tab[, colSums(n_tab) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  cells <- ifelse(n_tab == 0, "", n_tab)
  cat("\n\n")
  export_as(table = "patients_per_group_and_category")
  print(kable(cells, align = "c", caption = paste(
    "Patients per group and category (a patient can have samples in several",
    "categories). The control is in the boxplots only.")))
  cat("\n\n")

  # Samples per group, rule by rule, down to what each part of the report uses.
  grp <- function(x) table(factor(x$status, NB_STATUS))
  classified <- cohort[!is.na(cohort$status), ]
  in_matrix <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
    setNames(names(nb_matrices), paste("in", names(nb_matrices))),
    function(f) grp(classified[classified$omics_id %in% nb_matrices[[f]], ])))
  flow <- rbind(`in the sample sheet` = grp(classified), in_matrix,
                `kept, every rule above` = grp(used),
                `in the ATRX-interactor boxplots` = grp(box_samples),
                `in the differential expression` = grp(nb_de_samples))
  export_as(table = "samples_per_group_step_by_step")
  print(kable(flow, caption = paste(
    "Samples per group, step by step. The last two rows differ only by the",
    "control.")))
  cat("\n\n")

  # Every sample left out, by reason; matrix columns missing from the sheet
  # are listed too.
  ex <- cohort[!is.na(cohort$reason), ]
  lev <- unique(c(sort(unique(ex$reason[startsWith(ex$reason, "not in ")])),
                  "no classification",
                  sort(unique(ex$reason[startsWith(ex$reason, "classification:")])),
                  NB_REASONS))
  ex_tab <- data.frame(reason = lev[lev %in% ex$reason])
  ex_tab$n <- vapply(ex_tab$reason, function(r) sum(ex$reason == r), integer(1))
  ex_tab$samples <- vapply(ex_tab$reason, function(r)
    paste(sort(ex$omics_id[ex$reason == r]), collapse = ", "), character(1))
  cols <- unique(unlist(nb_matrices))
  no_meta <- setdiff(cols[!grepl("^(MNC|CL)_", cols)], nb_meta$omics_id)
  if (length(no_meta)) ex_tab <- rbind(ex_tab, data.frame(
    reason = paste("not in", basename(params$nb_metadata)), n = length(no_meta),
    samples = paste(sort(no_meta), collapse = ", ")))
  ex_tab <- rbind(ex_tab, data.frame(reason = "<b>Total</b>",
                                     n = sprintf("<b>%d</b>", sum(ex_tab$n)), samples = ""))
  # HTML with borders: a plain markdown table has no cell rules.
  export_as(table = "samples_left_out")
  print(kable(ex_tab, format = "html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
              align = c("l", "r", "l"), col.names = c("Reason", "n", "Samples"),
              caption = "Samples left out of the whole report",
              table.attr = 'class="table table-bordered table-condensed"'))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Sample sets

The tumour samples are grouped into five sets, each a subset of the categories
above. The sets overlap: "All tumour" holds every tumour sample, "DTC all"
every bone-marrow sample. Each set is one
[differential-expression](#differential-expression-atrxdel-mycnamp-and-atrxwtmycnwt)
analysis, in which the three groups are compared pairwise, and one box per
group in the [ATRX-interactor](#atrx-interactors) plots.

```{r cohort-analyses, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(nb_de_samples)) {
  tab <- t(vapply(NB_SETS, function(set) {
    d <- nb_set_samples(nb_de_samples, set)
    g <- factor(d$status, NB_GROUPS)
    np <- tapply(d$patient, g, function(p) length(unique(p)))
    np[is.na(np)] <- 0
    c(if (is.null(set$categories)) "every tumour category" else
        paste(set$categories, collapse = ", "),
      sprintf("%d (%d)", as.integer(table(g)), as.integer(np)))
  }, character(length(NB_GROUPS) + 1)))
  colnames(tab) <- c("Categories", NB_GROUPS)
  rownames(tab) <- sprintf("%s (box: %s)", vapply(NB_SETS, `[[`, "", "title"),
                           vapply(NB_SETS, `[[`, "", "label"))
  cat("\n\n")
  export_as(table = "samples_per_set")
  print(kable(tab, align = "c", caption = paste(
    "Samples (patients) per set. A comparison needs at least 2 samples per group.")))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Sample overview

Every tumour sample of the differential expression (the control excluded), on
the 2,000 most variable genes:

- top row: `full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts.csv`, the values
  tested;
- bottom row: `full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts_liblayout_corrected.csv`,
  the layout-corrected file the boxplots use.

Both rows are taken as log2(max(value, 0) + 1). Colour: ATRX/MYCN group,
library layout, sample type. Shape: primary tumour or bone marrow (DTC).

```{r cohort-expression, results = "asis"}
# ── Expression as tested: log2, one row per gene symbol ──────────────────────
lx <- lx_corr <- nb_ens <- NULL
if (!is.null(nb_counts) && !is.null(nb_de_samples) && nrow(nb_de_samples)) {
  # The two matrices are not written alike: the gene ID column can be GeneID,
  # another name, or a blank header (row names written by write.csv). Any
  # non-numeric column is annotation, not a sample; the ID is GeneID or else
  # the first such column, the symbol gene_name or else looked up from the
  # corrected matrix (GeneID -> gene_name), else the ID itself.
  # Columns picked by position: nb_counts[[""]] cannot select a blank header.
  annot_i <- which(!vapply(nb_counts, is.numeric, logical(1)))
  annot <- names(nb_counts)[annot_i]
  id_i <- if ("GeneID" %in% annot) match("GeneID", names(nb_counts)) else
    annot_i[annot != "gene_name"][1]
  id_col <- names(nb_counts)[id_i]  # NA when there is no ID column
  gene_ids <- if (!is.na(id_i)) as.character(nb_counts[[id_i]]) else rownames(nb_counts)
  strip_version <- function(x) sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", x)
  gene_sym <- if ("gene_name" %in% annot) as.character(nb_counts$gene_name) else
    if (!is.null(nb_expr) && all(c("GeneID", "gene_name") %in% names(nb_expr)))
      nb_expr$gene_name[match(strip_version(gene_ids), strip_version(nb_expr$GeneID))] else
    rep(NA_character_, length(gene_ids))
  cat(sprintf("\nGene columns in `%s`: ID from %s, symbol from %s.\n\n",
              basename(params$nb_counts),
              if (is.na(id_col)) "the row names" else
                if (nzchar(id_col)) sprintf("`%s`", id_col) else "the unnamed first column",
              if ("gene_name" %in% annot) "`gene_name`" else
                if (!all(is.na(gene_sym))) "the corrected matrix (matched on gene ID)" else
                "nowhere (gene IDs used instead)"))

  raw <- as.matrix(nb_counts[, nb_de_samples$omics_id, drop = FALSE])
  storage.mode(raw) <- "double"
  # Expected linear (normalised counts or CPM), so log2(value + 1). The
  # sentence below gives the range, so a file already on a log scale shows up.
  cat(sprintf(paste0("\n%s: %s genes, %d samples, values %s to %s; ",
                     "log2(value + 1) taken%s.\n\n"),
              basename(params$nb_counts), format(nrow(raw), big.mark = ","), ncol(raw),
              format(signif(min(raw, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
              format(signif(max(raw, na.rm = TRUE), 3), big.mark = ","),
              if (any(raw < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) sprintf(
                ", after setting %s negative values to 0",
                format(sum(raw < 0, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ",")) else ""))
  if (max(raw, na.rm = TRUE) < 30)
    cat("\n> **Check the input scale:** no value above 30, so this file may",
        "already be on a log scale, in which case log2(value + 1) is wrong.\n\n")
  lx <- log2(pmax(raw, 0) + 1)
  sym <- ifelse(is.na(gene_sym) | !nzchar(gene_sym), gene_ids, gene_sym)
  # Symbols on several Ensembl IDs: keep the most expressed, so each gene is
  # ranked once in GSEA.
  o <- order(-rowMeans(lx))
  o <- o[!duplicated(sym[o])]
  nb_ens <- setNames(gene_ids[o], sym[o])
  lx <- lx[o, , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(lx) <- sym[o]
}
# The layout-corrected file, for the PCAs only, with the same transform as
# the boxplots.
if (!is.null(nb_expr) && !is.null(nb_de_samples)) {
  ids <- intersect(nb_de_samples$omics_id, colnames(nb_expr))
  lx_corr <- as.matrix(nb_expr[, ids, drop = FALSE])
  storage.mode(lx_corr) <- "double"
  lx_corr <- log2(pmax(lx_corr, 0) + 1)
}

# ── PCA ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# PCA of samples on the 2,000 most variable expressed genes of a log2 matrix:
# the counts as tested, or the layout-corrected file (for display only; the
# tests use the layout as a covariate instead). Samples missing from the
# matrix are left out of the plot.
nb_pca <- function(E, d, n_top = 2000) {
  d <- d[d$omics_id %in% colnames(E), , drop = FALSE]
  E <- E[, d$omics_id, drop = FALSE]
  E <- E[rowSums(E > NB_EXPR_MIN) >= 2, , drop = FALSE]
  v <- apply(E, 1, var)
  E <- E[order(-v)[seq_len(min(n_top, nrow(E)))], , drop = FALSE]
  pc <- prcomp(t(E))
  out <- data.frame(group = factor(d$status, NB_GROUPS), category = d$category,
                    layout = d$layout, tissue = sub(" .*$", "", d$category),
                    PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = pc$x[, 2])
  attr(out, "ve") <- 100 * pc$sdev[1:2]^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2)
  out
}
NB_PCA_LEGEND <- c(group = "ATRX/MYCN group", layout = "Library layout",
                   category = "Sample type")
nb_pca_panel <- function(pc, colour, title, values = NULL) {
  ve <- attr(pc, "ve")
  p <- ggplot(pc, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = .data[[colour]], shape = tissue)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(title = title, x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", ve[1]),
         y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", ve[2]), shape = NULL,
         colour = NB_PCA_LEGEND[[colour]]) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
  if (!is.null(values)) p <- p + scale_colour_manual(values = values, drop = TRUE)
  p
}
# Plots side by side as one image (heights matched, legends kept).
nb_row <- function(plots) do.call(cbind, c(lapply(plots, ggplotGrob), size = "max"))

if (!is.null(nb_de_samples)) {
  sources <- list(`normalised counts` = lx, `layout-corrected` = lx_corr)
  files <- c(`normalised counts` = "as_tested", `layout-corrected` = "layout_corrected")
  params_of <- c(`normalised counts` = "nb_counts", `layout-corrected` = "nb_expression")
  for (src in names(sources)) {
    if (is.null(sources[[src]])) {
      cat(sprintf("\n> No %s matrix (`params$%s`): this row is skipped.\n\n",
                  src, params_of[[src]]))
      next
    }
    pc <- nb_pca(sources[[src]], nb_de_samples)
    lay <- sort(unique(pc$layout))
    show_plot(nb_row(list(
      nb_pca_panel(pc, "group", paste0("ATRX/MYCN group (", src, ")"), NB_GROUP_COL),
      nb_pca_panel(pc, "layout", paste0("Library layout (", src, ")"),
                   setNames(NB_LAYOUT_COL[seq_along(lay)], lay)),
      nb_pca_panel(pc, "category", paste0("Sample type (", src, ")")))),
      width = 13, height = 5, scroll = TRUE, name = paste0("overview_pca_", files[[src]]))
  }
}
```

# ATRX interactors

A proteomics co-immunoprecipitation experiment and an analysis 
by Celine Prakash identified proteins interacting with `ATRX_FL` or `ATRX_IFF`. 
To identify direct interactors (as opposed to indirect binding through complexes),  
Magdalena Rados tested the interactions of the top hits with ATRX FL/IFF in-silico
using AlphaFold2. The interactors are listed per construct: `ATRX_FL` only,
`ATRX_IFF` only, or shared by both
(`analysis/atrx_interactors/atrx_interactors.tsv`).
Here, we investigate the expression of the genes encoding these interactors, first in our
SK-N-SH lines, then in the [patient cohort](#patient-cohort), grouped by ATRX and MYCN status
and by the five [sample sets](#sample-sets) of the differential expression.

Each row is one gene: the four E6-derived SK-N-SH conditions on the left
(log2 normalised counts + 1), the patient groups on the right (log2 of the
layout-corrected values + 1). Each group has one box per sample set (All
tumour, Tum dx, DTC all, DTC dx, DTC rel) and the control one box; the sets
overlap, so a patient appears in several boxes. Within a box, a patient's
samples are averaged into one point (e.g. the Tum dx and DTC samples of one
patient in "All tumour"); the count under each box is in patients.


```{r atrx-data, results = "asis"}
# ── Inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The interactor list lives in this repository; resolve it from the Rmd's own
# path, since the Snakemake rule knits from a temporary directory.
atrx_tsv <- if (nzchar(params$atrx_interactors)) params$atrx_interactors else
  file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", "analysis",
            "atrx_interactors", "atrx_interactors.tsv")
ai <- if (file.exists(atrx_tsv)) read.delim(atrx_tsv, colClasses = "character") else NULL
if (is.null(ai)) cat("\n> **Not available.** `", atrx_tsv, "` was not found.\n\n", sep = "")

# SK-N-SH: the normalised counts of the cell-line report's "Genes of interest",
# from the fit on the 12 E6-derived samples (DESeq2.sample_sets E6only), so
# TP53 is neither plotted nor part of the normalisation.
nc <- grab("deseq2", "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL_E6only", "normalized_counts.csv")
if (is.null(nc)) missing_note("deseq2", "ATRX_IFF_vs_ATRX_FL_E6only", "normalized_counts.csv")

# Patients: the samples selected in "Patient cohort" (box_samples), on the
# layout-corrected matrix.
pat <- cell <- NULL
if (!is.null(nb_expr) && !is.null(box_samples) && !is.null(ai)) {
  # One row per sample and box: the tumour samples once per set they belong
  # to, the control in its own box.
  in_box <- function(d, label) { d$box <- rep(label, nrow(d)); d }
  tum <- box_samples[box_samples$status %in% NB_TUMOUR, ]
  keep <- do.call(rbind, c(
    lapply(NB_SETS, function(set) in_box(nb_set_samples(tum, set), set$label)),
    list(in_box(box_samples[box_samples$status %in% "control", ], "control"))))
  rownames(keep) <- NULL
  NB_BOX <- c(vapply(NB_SETS, `[[`, "", "label"), "control")

  # Interactor rows: Ensembl ID first, then the symbol, then previous symbols.
  ens <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", nb_expr$GeneID)
  rows <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ai)), function(i) {
    prev <- trimws(strsplit(ai$previous_symbols[i], ";")[[1]])
    hit <- c(which(ens == ai$ensembl_gene_id[i]),
             which(nb_expr$gene_name == ai$gene[i]),
             which(nb_expr$gene_name %in% prev[nzchar(prev)]))
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_integer_
  }, integer(1))
  vals <- as.matrix(nb_expr[rows[!is.na(rows)], box_samples$omics_id, drop = FALSE])
  n_neg <- sum(vals < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_neg) cat(sprintf(paste(
    "\nNegative values after the layout correction, set to 0 before",
    "log2(value + 1): %d.\n\n"), n_neg))
  pat <- data.frame(gene = rep(ai$gene[!is.na(rows)], times = ncol(vals)),
                    omics_id = rep(box_samples$omics_id, each = nrow(vals)),
                    value = log2(pmax(as.vector(vals), 0) + 1)) %>%
    inner_join(keep[, c("omics_id", "status", "box", "patient")], by = "omics_id",
               relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    group_by(gene, status, box, patient) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(key = factor(paste(status, box, sep = "|"),
                        levels = paste(rep(NB_STATUS, each = length(NB_BOX)),
                                       NB_BOX, sep = "|")),
           status = factor(status, NB_STATUS))
}

# SK-N-SH, log2(normalised counts + 1); the epicode GTF names genes by symbol.
if (!is.null(nc) && !is.null(meta) && !is.null(ai)) {
  ids <- tolower(nc$gene_id)
  crow <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(ai)), function(i) {
    cand <- tolower(c(ai$gene[i], trimws(strsplit(ai$previous_symbols[i], ";")[[1]])))
    hit <- match(cand[nzchar(cand)], ids)
    if (any(!is.na(hit))) hit[!is.na(hit)][1] else NA_integer_
  }, integer(1))
  cell <- nc[crow[!is.na(crow)], , drop = FALSE] %>%
    mutate(gene = ai$gene[!is.na(crow)]) %>% select(-gene_id) %>%
    pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "sample", values_to = "value") %>%
    inner_join(meta, by = "sample") %>%
    mutate(value = log2(value + 1), condition = cond_factor(as.character(condition)))
}

# ── One row per gene ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SK-N-SH on the left on its own y-axis, the patient groups on the right on
# one shared y-axis: two plots joined side by side, since one facet grid cannot
# give a single panel its own y-axis. Patient boxes are blue for tumour
# samples and grey for the tumour-free control, so the condition colours
# stay unique to SK-N-SH.
ATRX_FILL  <- c(tumour = "#6D8AB6", control = "#D9D9D9")
atrx_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8.5, colour = "grey20"),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "grey30"),
        strip.text   = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = "grey80"),
        plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 2, 4))

# Median line colour for a box fill: white where the fill is dark (relative
# luminance < 0.179, where white contrasts more than black), else the outline
# grey. A grey median vanishes on E6 and ATRX_FL.
median_ink <- function(fill) {
  v <- grDevices::col2rgb(fill) / 255
  v <- ifelse(v <= 0.03928, v / 12.92, ((v + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  ifelse(colSums(v * c(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722)) < 0.179, "white", "grey25")
}

# empty = TRUE draws the same panels without data, for a gene missing from one
# dataset only, so every row keeps the same layout.
atrx_boxes <- function(p, empty = FALSE) {
  if (empty) return(p + geom_blank() + atrx_theme +
                      theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()))
  p + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.62, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey25") +
    stat_summary(aes(colour = after_scale(median_ink(fill))), fun = median,
                 fun.min = median, fun.max = median, geom = "errorbar",
                 width = 0.62, linewidth = 0.45, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.13, height = 0, seed = 1),
               shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "grey15", size = 0.9, stroke = 0.3) +
    atrx_theme
}

atrx_cell_plot <- function(d, title, empty = FALSE) {
  atrx_boxes(ggplot(transform(d, panel = "SK-N-SH"),
                    aes(condition, value, fill = condition)), empty) +
    facet_grid(. ~ panel, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PAL) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = "log2(norm. counts + 1)")
}

atrx_patient_plot <- function(d, title = NULL, empty = FALSE) {
  n <- table(droplevels(d$key))
  lab <- sub("^.*\\|", "", names(n))
  if (!empty) lab <- sprintf("%s (%d)", lab, n)
  atrx_boxes(ggplot(d, aes(key, value,
                           fill = ifelse(status == "control", "control", "tumour"))), empty) +
    facet_grid(. ~ status, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = setNames(lab, names(n))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = ATRX_FILL) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = "log2(corrected value + 1)")
}

atrx_rows <- function(list_name) {
  if (is.null(ai) || (is.null(cell) && is.null(pat))) return(invisible())
  genes <- ai[ai$list == list_name, ]
  absent <- setdiff(genes$gene, c(cell$gene, pat$gene))
  if (length(absent)) cat("\nNot found in either dataset:",
                          paste(absent, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")
  # Layout templates for a gene missing from one dataset only.
  cell_blank <- if (!is.null(cell)) transform(cell[cell$gene == cell$gene[1], ], value = 0)
  pat_blank  <- if (!is.null(pat)) mutate(filter(pat, gene == gene[1]), value = 0)
  for (i in which(!genes$gene %in% absent)) {
    g  <- genes$gene[i]
    dc <- cell[cell$gene == g, ]
    dp <- pat[pat$gene == g, ]
    title <- g
    if (!is.null(cell) && !nrow(dc)) title <- paste0(title, "   ·   below the count filter in SK-N-SH")
    if (!is.null(pat) && !nrow(dp))  title <- paste0(title, "   ·   not in the patient matrix")
    left  <- if (!is.null(cell))
      atrx_cell_plot(if (nrow(dc)) dc else cell_blank, title, empty = !nrow(dc))
    right <- if (!is.null(pat))
      atrx_patient_plot(if (nrow(dp)) dp else pat_blank,
                        title = if (is.null(cell)) title, empty = !nrow(dp))
    if (is.null(left) || is.null(right)) {
      print(if (is.null(left)) right else left)
      next
    }
    grid::grid.newpage()
    grid::grid.draw(cbind(ggplotGrob(left), ggplotGrob(right), size = "max"))
  }
}
```

# Differential expression: ATRXdel, MYCNamp and ATRXwtMYCNwt

Genome-wide differential expression between the three tumour groups of the
[patient cohort](#patient-cohort), tested pairwise: **ATRXdel vs MYCNamp**,
**ATRXdel vs ATRXwtMYCNwt** and **MYCNamp vs ATRXwtMYCNwt**. Each comparison is
run five times:
- every tumour sample together;
- primary tumours at diagnosis (Tum dx);
- every bone-marrow sample pooled (DTC, all timepoints);
- bone marrow at diagnosis (DTC dx);
- bone marrow at relapse (DTC rel).

The control bone marrow is left out: it is not the same cells, so it is not
compared against. Groups,
categories and excluded samples are the ones defined in the
[patient cohort](#patient-cohort), with the samples per analysis in
[Sample sets](#sample-sets); the interactor boxplots use the same five sets.

**Data.** The normalised counts from the same reanalysis, *without* the
library-layout correction (`full_omics_expression_data_normalized_counts.csv`).
The interactor boxplots use the corrected matrix, but `removeBatchEffect` output is
meant for plotting, not for testing: the fit would not know that degrees of
freedom were spent on the layout, so p-values would come out too small
([limma `removeBatchEffect` help page](https://rdrr.io/bioc/limma/man/removebatcheffect.html)).
The library layout (`library_layout` in `metadata_table_wStage.xlsx`) is put in
the model instead.

**Model.** [limma](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkv007) on log2(normalised
counts + 1). It uses the "limma-trend" approach of
[Law et al. 2014](https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2014-15-2-r29) for log-counts:
an empirical Bayes variance trend on mean expression, with robust hyperparameters.
The design is `~ 0 + group + layout`, plus the sample category (Tum dx, Tum TRE,
DTC dx, …) in the two pooled analyses. A covariate is dropped in an analysis
where it has a single level. In the combined analysis, category is coded so
that each tumour group's estimate is its average over the tumour categories
(sum-to-zero coding). Where one patient contributes several samples (as in the
pooled analyses), the patient is a blocking factor, with the within-patient
correlation estimated by `duplicateCorrelation`
([Smyth et al. 2005](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/bti270)). Each
analysis tests only genes with a value above 1 in at least as many samples as
its smallest group. Significant genes: BH-adjusted p < `r params$padj` and
|log2FC| ≥ `r params$lfc`, the thresholds used everywhere in this report.

**Enrichment.** [fgsea](https://doi.org/10.1101/060012) on the genes ranked by
the limma moderated t. The collections are MSigDB
[Hallmark](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2015.12.004) and GO biological process
(via `msigdbr`), and KEGG. Plots and tables follow the
GSEA section of the cell-line report: significant pathways only (padj <
`r params$padj`), the top 12 by |NES| on each side. The complete results,
significant or not, are in the exported tables.

**Pathways across groups.** Each analysis opens with one test per pathway
instead of one per pair. Every pathway gets a score per sample from
[GSVA](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-14-7) (Gaussian kernel, on the same
log2 values). limma then fits the design above to the scores, and a moderated
F-test ([Smyth 2004](https://doi.org/10.2202/1544-6115.1027)) asks whether the
three tumour groups differ at all. Post-hoc pairwise differences show which
groups drive it. Because this tests samples rather than genes, correlation
between the genes of a set does not inflate it. fgsea's gene-permutation
p-values below are inflated by that correlation, increasingly so for large sets
([Wu & Smyth 2012](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gks461)). The F-test is
therefore the better guide to how strongly a pathway separates the groups.

**Direction.** In "A vs B", log2FC > 0 and NES > 0 mean higher in A.

Every comparison is also exported: the volcano and enrichment plots as PDFs under
`figures/patients/`, and the full limma and fgsea results plus the up/down gene lists as
CSVs under `tables/patients/`. Both sit in one folder per analysis (`all_combined`,
`tumour_dx`, `BM_pooled`, `BM_dx`, `BM_relapse`).

**Checks.** The overview PCA of every tumour sample is in
[Sample overview](#sample-overview). Each comparison opens with a QC line and
two plots:
- the number of samples and patients per group;
- the histogram of raw p-values ([Robinson 2014](http://varianceexplained.org/statistics/interpreting-pvalue-histogram/)):
  flat means no signal, a spike at 0 means signal, a pile-up near 1 means the
  model fits poorly;
- a PCA of the two groups' samples alone, on the layout-corrected file.


```{r patient-de, results = "asis"}
# ── Comparisons ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Groups, analyses (NB_SETS), samples (nb_de_samples) and the log2 matrices
# (lx tested, lx_corr for the PCAs) are set up in "Patient cohort".
NB_PAIRS  <- list(c("ATRXdel", "MYCNamp"), c("ATRXdel", "ATRXwtMYCNwt"),
                  c("MYCNamp", "ATRXwtMYCNwt"))

nbde <- NULL
pkgs <- c("limma", "fgsea", "msigdbr", "GSVA")
pkgs_ok <- vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(pkgs_ok)) {
  cat("\n> **Not available.** R package(s)", paste(pkgs[!pkgs_ok], collapse = ", "),
      "missing; see `workflow/envs/report.yaml`.\n\n")
} else if (is.null(lx)) {
  cat("\n> **Not available.** `params$nb_counts` or `params$nb_metadata` was not",
      "found; this section is skipped.\n\n")
} else {
  # ── Gene sets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  msig <- function(category, subcategory = NULL) {
    m <- if (is.null(subcategory)) msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = category)
         else msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = category,
                               subcategory = subcategory)
    split(m$gene_symbol, m$gs_name)
  }
  # The pipeline's current-KEGG GMT if this run built it (Run.gsea with
  # KEGG_CURRENT), else MSigDB's frozen ~2011 KEGG.
  kegg_gmt <- file.path(OUT, "resources", "generated_gmts", "kegg_current.gmt")
  NB_COLLECTIONS <- list(
    Hallmark = msig("H"),
    KEGG = if (file.exists(kegg_gmt)) fgsea::gmtPathways(kegg_gmt) else msig("C2", "CP:KEGG"),
    `GO:BP` = msig("C5", "GO:BP"))
  # msigdbr lists a symbol once per Entrez ID, so some sets repeat a gene.
  NB_COLLECTIONS <- lapply(NB_COLLECTIONS, function(sets) lapply(sets, unique))
  cat(sprintf("\nKEGG gene sets: %s.\n\n", if (file.exists(kegg_gmt))
    "current KEGG (`resources/generated_gmts/kegg_current.gmt`)" else
    "MSigDB C2:CP:KEGG (the pipeline's current-KEGG GMT was not found)"))

  # ── Pathways across the tumour groups: GSVA scores, moderated F ────────────
  # One GSVA score per pathway and sample, on this analysis's samples, then
  # the same limma design as the genes.
  # The F-test asks whether the tumour groups differ at all (contrasts among
  # them). Being a test across samples, it is
  # not inflated by correlation between the genes of a set, unlike fgsea's
  # gene-permutation p-values. Scores need no trend: robust eBayes only.
  nb_pathway_anova <- function(E, sets, X, d, tum) {
    capture.output(S <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(GSVA::gsva(
      GSVA::gsvaParam(E, sets, minSize = params$gsea_min_size,
                      maxSize = params$gsea_max_size, kcdf = "Gaussian"),
      verbose = FALSE, BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam()))))
    fit <- if (anyDuplicated(d$patient)) {
      corr <- limma::duplicateCorrelation(S, X, block = d$patient)$consensus.correlation
      limma::lmFit(S, X, block = d$patient, correlation = corr)
    } else limma::lmFit(S, X)
    contrast <- function(a, b) {
      v <- setNames(rep(0, ncol(X)), colnames(X))
      v[make.names(a)] <- 1; v[make.names(b)] <- -1
      v
    }
    # F over the tumour groups: the first against each of the others.
    # cbind, not sapply: with two groups sapply would return a plain vector.
    cm_f <- do.call(cbind, lapply(tum[-1], function(b) contrast(tum[1], b)))
    tt <- limma::topTable(limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit, cm_f), robust = TRUE),
                          coef = seq_len(ncol(cm_f)), number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
    out <- data.frame(pathway = rownames(S),
                      size = vapply(sets[rownames(S)], function(g) sum(g %in% rownames(E)), 0L),
                      F = if ("F" %in% names(tt)) tt$F else tt$t^2,
                      pvalue = tt$P.Value, padj = tt$adj.P.Val, check.names = FALSE)
    # Raw group means of the score (for display).
    grp <- factor(d$status, NB_GROUPS)
    for (g in levels(droplevels(grp)))
      out[[paste("mean", g)]] <- rowMeans(S[, grp == g, drop = FALSE])
    # Post hoc: every pair of tumour groups, BH within each pair.
    pairs <- utils::combn(tum, 2, simplify = FALSE)
    cm_p <- do.call(cbind, lapply(pairs, function(pr) contrast(pr[1], pr[2])))
    f_p <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit, cm_p), robust = TRUE)
    for (k in seq_along(pairs)) {
      tk <- limma::topTable(f_p, coef = k, number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
      lab <- paste(pairs[[k]], collapse = " - ")
      out[[paste("diff", lab)]] <- tk$logFC
      out[[paste("padj", lab)]] <- tk$adj.P.Val
    }
    out <- out[order(out$pvalue), ]
    rownames(out) <- NULL  # else the CSV repeats the pathway as a row-name column
    out
  }

  # ── One limma fit per analysis, the three pairs as contrasts ───────────────
  nb_fit <- function(d) {
    grp <- factor(d$status, NB_GROUPS)
    n_grp <- table(grp)
    X <- model.matrix(~ 0 + grp)
    colnames(X) <- make.names(levels(grp))
    terms <- "~ 0 + group"
    # Category in sum-to-zero coding: each group's coefficient is its mean
    # over the categories. Group-vs-group contrasts do not depend on the
    # coding; it only keeps the group coefficients interpretable.
    cat_f <- factor(d$category)
    if (nlevels(cat_f) > 1) {
      C <- contr.sum(nlevels(cat_f))[as.integer(cat_f), , drop = FALSE]
      C[is.na(cat_f), ] <- 0
      colnames(C) <- paste0("category:", levels(cat_f)[-nlevels(cat_f)])
      X <- cbind(X, C)
      terms <- paste(terms, "+ category")
    }
    lay_f <- factor(d$layout)
    if (nlevels(lay_f) > 1) {
      L <- model.matrix(~ lay_f)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
      colnames(L) <- paste0("layout:", levels(lay_f)[-1])
      X <- cbind(X, L)
      terms <- paste(terms, "+ layout")
    }
    X <- X[, colSums(X != 0) > 0, drop = FALSE]  # groups absent here
    ne <- limma::nonEstimable(X)
    if (length(ne)) X <- X[, setdiff(colnames(X), ne), drop = FALSE]
    n_min <- max(2, min(n_grp[n_grp > 0]))
    E <- lx[, d$omics_id, drop = FALSE]
    E <- E[rowSums(E > NB_EXPR_MIN) >= n_min, , drop = FALSE]
    corr <- NA
    if (anyDuplicated(d$patient)) {
      corr <- limma::duplicateCorrelation(E, X, block = d$patient)$consensus.correlation
      fit <- limma::lmFit(E, X, block = d$patient, correlation = corr)
    } else {
      fit <- limma::lmFit(E, X)
    }
    res <- list()
    skipped <- character()
    for (pr in NB_PAIRS) {
      a <- make.names(pr[1]); b <- make.names(pr[2])
      if (any(n_grp[pr] < 2) || !all(c(a, b) %in% colnames(X))) {
        skipped <- c(skipped, sprintf("%s vs %s (%s)", pr[1], pr[2], paste(
          sprintf("%s: %d", pr, as.integer(n_grp[pr])), collapse = ", ")))
        next
      }
      cm <- matrix(0, ncol(X), 1, dimnames = list(colnames(X), NULL))
      cm[a, 1] <- 1; cm[b, 1] <- -1
      f2 <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit, cm), trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
      tt <- limma::topTable(f2, coef = 1, number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
      de <- data.frame(gene_id = rownames(tt), ensembl_id = unname(nb_ens[rownames(tt)]),
                       AveExpr = tt$AveExpr, log2FoldChange = tt$logFC, stat = tt$t,
                       pvalue = tt$P.Value, padj = tt$adj.P.Val)
      st <- sort(setNames(de$stat, de$gene_id), decreasing = TRUE)
      gs <- lapply(NB_COLLECTIONS, function(sets) {
        set.seed(1)
        # capture.output: fgsea's progress bar would print into this asis chunk.
        utils::capture.output(g <- suppressWarnings(fgsea::fgsea(
          sets, st, minSize = params$gsea_min_size, maxSize = params$gsea_max_size,
          nproc = 1)))
        g <- as.data.frame(g[order(g$padj), ])
        g$leadingEdge <- vapply(g$leadingEdge, paste, "", collapse = ";")
        g
      })
      sel <- d$status %in% pr
      res[[paste(pr, collapse = " vs ")]] <- list(
        num = pr[1], den = pr[2], de = de, gsea = gs,
        pca = nb_pca(if (!is.null(lx_corr)) lx_corr else E, d[sel, ]))
    }
    tum <- NB_TUMOUR[n_grp[NB_TUMOUR] >= 2 & make.names(NB_TUMOUR) %in% colnames(X)]
    anova <- if (length(tum) >= 2)
      lapply(NB_COLLECTIONS, function(sets) nb_pathway_anova(E, sets, X, d, tum))
    list(n = n_grp, terms = terms, corr = corr, n_genes = nrow(E), res = res,
         skipped = skipped, anova = anova, anova_groups = tum,
         layouts = table(factor(d$status, NB_GROUPS), d$layout))
  }

  nbde <- lapply(NB_SETS, function(set) {
    d <- nb_set_samples(nb_de_samples, set)
    c(set, list(n_patients = tapply(d$patient, factor(d$status, NB_GROUPS),
                                    function(p) length(unique(p)))),
      if (nrow(d)) nb_fit(d))
  })
}

# ── Drawing one analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Significant genes in two scrollable lists side by side, ranked like
# top_genes(): -log10(padj) x |log2FC|.
nb_gene_lists <- function(r, num, den, base) {
  sig <- r %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj < params$padj,
                      abs(log2FoldChange) >= params$lfc) %>%
    mutate(score = -log10(padj) * abs(log2FoldChange)) %>% arrange(desc(score))
  side <- function(d, title, name) {
    cat('<div style="flex: 1 1 340px; min-width: 0;">\n\n')
    cat(sprintf("**%s** (%s genes)\n\n", title, format(nrow(d), big.mark = ",")))
    if (nrow(d)) {
      export_as(table = name)
      scroll_table(transmute(d, gene = gene_id, log2FC = round(log2FoldChange, 2),
                             padj = fmt_p(padj), AveExpr = round(AveExpr, 1)),
                   max_height = 320)
    } else cat("None.\n\n")
    cat("</div>\n\n")
  }
  cat('<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; column-gap: 1.5em;">\n\n')
  side(filter(sig, log2FoldChange > 0), paste("Higher in", num),
       paste0(base, "_higher_in_", gsub(" ", "_", num)))
  side(filter(sig, log2FoldChange < 0), paste("Higher in", den),
       paste0(base, "_higher_in_", gsub(" ", "_", den)))
  cat("</div>\n\n")
}

# Pathway F-test: heatmap of the group means of the significant pathways (top
# NB_ANOVA_TOP by p), then
# the same pathways as a table with the post-hoc pairwise differences.
NB_ANOVA_TOP <- 30
nb_anova_show <- function(a, coll, title, tum, base) {
  slug <- gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", coll)
  export_table(a, name = paste0(base, "pathway_Ftest_", slug, "_all"))
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s**: %d of %d pathways differ among the tumour groups (padj < %s).\n\n",
              coll, sum(a$padj < params$padj), nrow(a), params$padj))
  sig <- head(a[a$padj < params$padj, , drop = FALSE], NB_ANOVA_TOP)
  if (!nrow(sig)) return(invisible())
  sig$pathway <- sub("^(HALLMARK|GOBP)_", "", sig$pathway)
  means <- grep("^mean ", names(sig), value = TRUE)
  # Rows ranked by the ATRXdel - MYCNamp difference (highest in ATRXdel on
  # top), or by the first pair's difference when one of the two is absent.
  rank_col <- if ("diff ATRXdel - MYCNamp" %in% names(sig)) "diff ATRXdel - MYCNamp" else
    grep("^diff ", names(sig), value = TRUE)[1]
  sig <- sig[order(-sig[[rank_col]]), ]
  long <- sig %>% select(pathway, all_of(means)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-pathway, names_to = "group", values_to = "score") %>%
    mutate(group = factor(sub("^mean ", "", group), NB_GROUPS),
           pathway = factor(pathway, rev(sig$pathway)))
  lim <- max(abs(long$score))
  p <- ggplot(long, aes(group, pathway, fill = score)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#0d366b", mid = "white", high = "#B72656",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-lim, lim), name = "mean GSVA\nscore") +
    labs(title = paste0(coll, ": ", title, ", pathways across the tumour groups"),
         subtitle = sprintf("F-test padj < %s, top %d by p; rows ranked by %s",
                            params$padj, nrow(sig), sub("^diff ", "", rank_col)),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
  show_enrich(p, sig$pathway, nrow(sig) + 2, panel_width = 0.7 * nlevels(droplevels(long$group)),
              name = paste0(base, "pathway_Ftest_", slug))
  # The table: F, padj, then each pair's difference with its padj in brackets.
  tab <- data.frame(pathway = sig$pathway, size = sig$size, F = round(sig$F, 1),
                    padj = fmt_p(sig$padj), check.names = FALSE)
  for (m in means) tab[[sub("^mean ", "", m)]] <- round(sig[[m]], 2)
  for (dcol in grep("^diff ", names(sig), value = TRUE)) {
    lab <- sub("^diff ", "", dcol)
    tab[[lab]] <- sprintf("%.2f (%s)", sig[[dcol]], fmt_p(sig[[paste("padj", lab)]]))
  }
  export_as(table = paste0(base, "pathway_Ftest_", slug))
  scroll_table(tab)
}

# QC for one comparison: group sizes, the raw p-value histogram, and a PCA of
# the two groups' samples.
nb_qc <- function(r, x, base) {
  g2 <- c(r$num, r$den)
  ns <- as.integer(x$n[g2]); np <- as.integer(x$n_patients[g2])
  cat(sprintf("\n**QC.** Samples (patients): %s %d (%d), %s %d (%d). %s genes tested.\n\n",
              g2[1], ns[1], np[1], g2[2], ns[2], np[2],
              format(nrow(r$de), big.mark = ",")))
  h <- ggplot(r$de, aes(pvalue)) +
    geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.02), fill = "#6D8AB6", colour = "white",
                   linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(r$de) / 50, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.3) +
    labs(title = "Raw p-values", subtitle = "dashed: expected if no gene differs",
         x = "p-value", y = "genes") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"))
  pc <- nb_pca_panel(r$pca, "group", sprintf("PCA of the two groups (%s)",
                     if (is.null(lx_corr)) "as tested" else "layout-corrected file"),
                     NB_GROUP_COL)
  show_plot(nb_row(list(h, pc)), width = 9.4, height = 4.6, name = paste0(base, "_qc"))
}

nb_show <- function(key) {
  x <- nbde[[key]]
  if (is.null(x)) return(invisible())
  if (!length(x$res)) {
    cat("\n> No comparison possible: fewer than 2 samples in every pair of groups.\n\n")
    return(invisible())
  }
  cat(sprintf("\nModel `%s`, %s genes tested%s.\n\n", x$terms,
              format(x$n_genes, big.mark = ","),
              if (is.na(x$corr)) "" else sprintf(
                "; patients blocked, within-patient correlation %.2f", x$corr)))
  print(kable(as.data.frame.matrix(x$layouts), caption = "Samples per library layout"))
  cat("\n\n")
  if (length(x$skipped))
    cat("\n> **Skipped, fewer than 2 samples in a group:**",
        paste(x$skipped, collapse = "; "), "\n\n")
  if (!is.null(x$anova)) {
    cat("\n\n### Pathways across the tumour groups\n\n")
    cat(sprintf(paste0("\nGSVA score per pathway and sample; moderated F-test across %s ",
                       "(same design as above). Colour: mean score per group. Post-hoc ",
                       "columns: difference in mean score (padj).\n\n"),
                paste(x$anova_groups, collapse = ", ")))
    for (coll in names(x$anova))
      nb_anova_show(x$anova[[coll]], coll, x$title, x$anova_groups, paste0(key, "/"))
  }
  for (pr in names(x$res)) {
    r <- x$res[[pr]]
    base <- file.path(key, gsub(" ", "_", pr))
    cat("\n\n###", pr, "\n\n")
    nb_qc(r, x, base)
    export_table(r$de, name = paste0(base, "_limma_all_genes"))
    show_plot(volcano(r$de, paste0(x$title, ": ", pr), num = r$num, den = r$den),
              width = 8.4, height = 6.2, name = paste0(base, "_volcano"))
    nb_gene_lists(r$de, r$num, r$den, base)
    for (coll in names(r$gsea)) {
      g <- r$gsea[[coll]]
      slug <- gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", coll)
      export_table(g, name = paste0(base, "_gsea_", slug, "_all"))
      cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s**\n\n", coll))
      g <- mutate(g, numerator = r$num, denominator = r$den,
                  pathway = sub("^GOBP_", "", pathway))
      export_as(plot = paste0(base, "_gsea_", slug), table = paste0(base, "_gsea_", slug))
      gsea_dot(g, paste0(coll, ": ", x$title, ", ", pr))
      export_as()  # gsea_dot draws nothing when no pathway is significant
    }
  }
}
```

```{r export-figures, include = FALSE}
# Last chunk: copy the PDFs knitr's second device saved next to each embedded
# PNG (<label>-<n>.pdf) into figures/<section>/. Chunks drawn through
# show_plot() have already written theirs.
if (EXPORT) {
  # rmarkdown hands knitr an absolute fig.path; a relative one is resolved
  # against knitr's base or output directory.
  fig_dir <- dirname(knitr::fig_path(".pdf"))
  if (!grepl("^(/|[A-Za-z]:)", fig_dir))
    fig_dir <- file.path(c(knitr::opts_knit$get("base.dir"),
                           knitr::opts_knit$get("output.dir"), getwd()), fig_dir)
  src <- unique(list.files(unique(fig_dir), pattern = "\\.pdf$", full.names = TRUE))
  for (f in src) {
    label <- sub("-[0-9]+\\.pdf$", "", basename(f))
    dest <- file.path(FIG_DIR, cur_section(label))
    dir.create(dest, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    file.copy(f, file.path(dest, basename(f)), overwrite = TRUE)
  }
}
```
